claims.statement: The right Collaboration panel keeps recorded exchanges and pending response requests visible across chats; expanding an exchange preserves the active chat and draft, while the bottom Dock presents Agent relationships.
Native material panels retain GPUI state and input ownership while AppKit supplies composition and attached-window focus handling.
Background archive-read failures preserve the last confirmed state; explicit failed checks show local feedback.

Conversation selection is read-only and shares one selection document across the text blocks of a rendered message. Copy controls show transient success feedback; selection does not span all messages.

The menu controller makes its nonactivating panel key on open without application-wide activation, and lifecycle tests require unchanged foreground application identity and a hidden workspace that remains hidden.

Native account disclosures use one Core Animation transaction to move and reveal account rows; the canvas accommodates both animation endpoints and requests the screen refresh rate without per-frame window resizing.

GPUI notifications prioritize errors, warnings and information for the bell and badge. Shared status rows use severity color with an icon and explicit wording; native menu-bar feedback keeps its compact icon and colored explanatory popover.

GPUI account problems use shared inline feedback beside the affected account without requiring a popup. Native menu-bar account feedback retains its compact icon and explanatory popover, whose closure does not clear the source.

Work results in global command search open their existing owner conversation with scoped evidence and business ownership; conversations, global Collaboration and Graph remain separate, while Guardian settings and per-conversation evidence keep their existing owners.
Selected Work and private reviewer records load separately from bounded overview previews, retain explicit source and size limits, and do not treat cache or native completion as Work acceptance.

Pause Work blocks new contributions and completion without rolling back native execution; the global Save review details switch only controls observation and does not change native execution permissions.
Each independent Agent owns its displayed composer, and submitted input targets that Agent's saved conversation instead of the first root.

The existing desktop exposes explicit read-only Memory summary and Actual usage views in Agent preferences, and Actual usage in selected Work details. Source changes discard old views; copying is explicit. Unknown and shared usage and delivery versus assessment remain separate facts.

Archived and blocked conversations keep the normal locked input bar and center the shared status and recovery controls within it. The unsent draft stays saved internally and returns after recovery; the blocked bar does not repeat its text or show a duplicate status band.

Agent preferences lists at most the newest 100 retained Decodex attached-branch receipts for the exact source. Verified branch navigation preserves the source draft, uncertain creation is not repeated, and archived branches require native restoration before refresh.

Shift-Esc targets Graph or conversation fullscreen through the persistent shell, including native composer forwarding. Graph fullscreen retains both sidebars; conversation fullscreen hides them and restores their requested visibility and widths on exit.
Parent-managed native chats expose Open parent; only failed native connections expose Retry. A positively unsent message keeps its own Not sent and Resend receipt in the scrolling transcript.
A locked conversation exposes Fork only for a readable prompt in the current native timeline binding. It creates and opens a native branch directly while preserving the original writer and draft.
Browsing or creating another conversation keeps the active call bound to its original owner and shows background call controls while preserving each conversation's draft.

The Graph groups recorded Project membership with a stable bottom rail and caption. Selecting a Project or one of its Agents highlights the rail and adds upper corners. Point overview omits small captions, and layout keeps clearance between Projects.
Settings supplies new independent conversation defaults; the input-bar shield selects current native permissions and the model menu includes speed, while native Subagents retain native inheritance.

The existing conversation browser and Project-grouped Work list have independent saved status filters with an explicit All statuses reset. They intersect existing Project and search predicates, keep a selected label when rows change, and retain exact navigation, drafts and evidence ownership without sending commands or changing native/business state.
The header groups native Side chats with their source. An ordinary source offers a new Side chat button. The personal Assistant omits this button and can still show existing branches.

Conversation actions use the short Fork label, with boundary, provider and no-send details in adjacent text. Persistent attached conversation surfaces use Side chat and Side chats; native protocol identifiers and Git branch terminology remain unchanged.

Fork uses arrow.triangle.branch; account routing uses point.topleft.down.to.point.bottomright.curvepath in GPUI and Menu Bar. Local fork records keep their identity suffixes. Project source tabs retain Main, personal source tabs use their conversation topic, and Side chat tabs use current topics with numbered labels before a title is available.

Fork, Retry and Unarchive share settings_button sizing, border, radius and interaction feedback. Status copy wraps within its rail. Fork starts creation after source preparation without a second confirmation or Cancel control; conversation progress and recovery use the band above the composer, and creation sends no message.

Nonblocking conversation feedback uses the band above the composer; send restrictions and archive status use the disabled composer. History retry and summary notices reuse shared inline feedback. Persistent and animated local feedback share a compact inset row with a quiet tone fill, icon and explicit wording, with text, icons and recovery actions vertically centered. Field and operation failures stay beside their controls, login-item and sleep-setting recovery actions stay inside their feedback rows, app-wide events use the notification center, whole-page startup failure uses the shared status row, and Menu Bar retains compact native feedback.

Assistant remains built in and always available. RAGFlow shares lifecycle controls, full version readback, details and inline feedback with other components. Install checks Docker and Compose and opens setup when no models are saved. The editor uses one shared OpenAI-compatible Base URL and optional masked API key with separate model IDs. Save verifies both models and initializes Memory. New connections enable automatic learning; existing saved choices survive updates.
RAGFlow setup uses the current local service profile and personal Assistant. Generated credentials and raw scope IDs are not Components fields.
Pending Assistant context confirmation is presented through shared inline feedback in Work, outside the RAGFlow connection editor.

The six Settings sections are General, Agents, Appearance, Components, Accounts and Diagnostics. They share a 620-point content column and normal App typography with visible descriptions. New conversations has two rows: Permissions shows its selected mode's meaning and all four explanations in the menu, while Speed uses the existing segmented control and selected-speed usage. Context defaults and Assistance retain their native settings owners. General contains Background controls and the app version with the native update action; Updates has no separate navigation entry.

RAGFlow's saved summary keeps Edit available and shows aligned shared Base URL, extraction model, embedding model and key status without exposing the key. Its editor has four fields in two columns. Empty required values disable Save and complete invalid input receives inline validation. A blank key retains the saved extraction connection key only at its unchanged Base URL. Collapse retains the draft; Cancel discards the draft and errors and returns to the expanded summary.

Settings uses shared quiet group surfaces, divided rows and distinct section, label, value and help roles. Ordinary setting names, component names and field labels use normal weight; section titles use medium weight and muted text. Accounts retains compact rows in one list surface. Component names, versions and lifecycle actions share a row. Expanded details use the shared inset surface. Model Save and Add account use shared primary buttons and feedback stays with its operation.

Local startup prepares Codex through the shared runtime preparation owner. Components has no permanent Verify or generic Retry action. An interrupted first download returns to Install. Reinstall is available for an installed private runtime and complete errors remain in expanded details. External container runtimes are not repaired.
Escape closes the open permission menu first. The workspace handles subsequent dismissal of the Settings overlay.
Settings uses shared section transitions and disclosure motion. Reduced motion applies to these transitions.

Each GPUI account summary places its identity, a fixed-width quota column and management actions on one compact row. One or two quota windows use the same summary height. Not-applicable windows are omitted while unknown usage keeps its row. Expanded activity retains a two-column label/value grid with current and best streak together, followed by the daily chart and a separate Reset cards area. Metric labels and values share the quota text size and muted color. Values use tabular figures without extra size or weight, and the daily chart uses a subdued accent.
The GPUI account summary owns the disclosure click target and hand cursor. Expanded activity is an ordinary reading area; clicking its metrics does not collapse the account.

Diagnostics shows one normal-size overall status flow and three group summaries before disclosure. Unchecked Codex checks are explicit without a redundant Run checks caption. Connection changes and recovery information remain explicit. Technical details retains every result and warns when a report is cached. Uniform groups share one status; mixed groups retain per-item statuses. Stale reports cannot supply current summaries or unchecked-check guidance; native process values keep aligned columns and explicit missing-value labels.

Appearance places all theme previews in the Settings page's single scroll area. Names wrap instead of truncating, and no inner theme scroll area captures wheel input. Color scheme help is shown when System is selected.

Component rows retain complete reported versions, including original prefixes, punctuation, build metadata and Git describe suffixes. The RAGFlow receipt and UI retain its server-reported version directly without a wrapper conversion or separate release-channel row.

Component status lights use existing runtime, plugin, Research and RAGFlow state and the selected theme's semantic tones. RAGFlow is Ready only with a responding public API and configured Memory; tooltip and accessibility text explain each light without a repeated status caption. Container recovery guidance stays inside the expanded details. Public checks run in the background on initial inspection and Components entry with a three-second limit and no model requests or loading rows.

Reset Memory requires inline confirmation bound to the exact reviewed managed Memory. It uses the native RAGFlow API to remove that Memory and create an empty replacement with saved models, preserves unrelated data and the current automatic-learning choice, and does not replay old conversations. A failed replacement leaves the private receipt without the deleted Memory identity and uses Edit and Save for recovery. Reset is not in-place reindexing or a physical-erasure guarantee.
The sidebar has a fixed Assistant entry and separate Chats and Projects sections. Pin provides shortcuts. Codex conversations and Archived stay below the scrolling directory.

Global Collaboration orders human requests before agent exchanges and opens explicit responses in source conversations. Its fixed-size toolbar icon retains a pending badge without visible text, while Graph stays available and starts closed.
Assistant opens its stable conversation. Conversation rows offer contextual pin, archive and deletion actions. Archived entries have restore and deletion actions.
Work summaries retain their existing 100-record service bound; the sidebar's complete rendering of available conversations and the global Work search do not remove that backend summary limit.
Command-K offers Open Assistant, New chat, New chat in project and the conversation catalogs. Selecting a result opens its destination through the workspace and preserves the draft.
Adding a project registers its folder. New chat in a project opens an independent conversation draft scoped to that project.
Archived opens a centered workspace overlay with native catalog actions to restore and delete conversations.

The sidebar keeps temporary hover visibility separate from its pinned preference. A 100 ms pointer dwell expands the rail, including after automatic collapse; leaving waits 220 ms, reentry cancels close, and section disclosure does not pin it. The full-height preview clips only the overlapping portion of Collaboration. The right panel keeps its allocation and uncovered controls stay visible and interactive.
Settings opens in the main Shell's shared overlay and restores workspace focus on dismissal.

The sidebar keeps its complete content canvas mounted at the expanded width through opening, closing and reversal while the outer panel clips it. The settled compact layout retains project and conversation initials, omits empty explanations and project-group spacing, and preserves the stored expansion choices.

Opt-in frame tracing records the sidebar's moving visible width and content width alongside CPU frame construction and submission timing; these measurements do not include GPU completion or display scanout.

The sidebar, activity islands, response-statistics popover and history previews reuse HoverIntent for 100 ms entry dwell, 220 ms departure grace and pending cancellation. A history tick group and its card form one target, and scrubbing updates the retained card immediately without repeated arrival.

A committed hover or explicit sidebar, activity-island or metrics toggle permits a bounded 400 ms transition in a visible inactive App without changing its background-rendering preference, while system reduced motion and VoiceOver remain authoritative.

The main window minimum is 480 by 360 points. PanelLayout reserves a 360-point reading width and 40-point rail, gives the left navigation fixed allocation priority, floats a right panel that cannot fit, and automatically collapses nonfitting full navigation while preserving its pinned preference for restoration.

Both sidebars render the original workspace_surface field color in the main GPUI window for docked, floating and compact navigation states, without separate native Liquid Glass hosts. The existing native input bar, activity-island and menu materials remain independent.

Work in progress is a read-only UI projection of unfinished unarchived scoped work and native agents, shown above the composer only for existing conversations while Graph is closed; it uses bounded scrolling and shared disclosure motion and opens existing conversations.
Work and Debug activity-island headers use distinct accent-tinted symbols measured through the shared icon slot and existing activity-island size tiers.

Closing and reversing a sidebar retain its docked or floating placement; animated width does not select a different placement or material. Rendering tests cover stable content geometry across allocation changes, interrupted closing and the retained compact rail.
Overlay glass style inherits Window glass style when no override exists and follows later changes, while explicit Regular and Clear choices remain independent.

Workspace pane foreground uses main-window geometry and retained presentations through ui_layout::pane, which reuses unchanged content and retains live accessibility geometry. Both content roots share system typography through workspace_panel_content.

The main-window sidebar routes pointer entry and departure through one shared HoverIntent owner in expanded and compact states. Entry starts the shared dwell even when the pointer stops without another unpressed mouse move.

Workspace panels retain their main-window presentation during placement and width changes, including the compact rail. State, activity animation and hover updates invalidate cached content, while sidebar keyboard actions use the main workspace.
The glass contour and foreground mask change in one Core Animation transaction with implicit actions disabled.

The compact rail and temporary left preview retain full height and the bottom Archived footer through automatic collapse and restoration. An explicitly pinned full left panel that must float, and the right floating panel, stop above the complete composer area. Floating panels mask covered reading-plane paint and pointer targets without reflow.

The native composer measures content at its current parent anchor width and has a single selected native material, without an additional GPUI fill or window backdrop; the editor and its focus remain owned by the existing composer.

A full-height left preview masks the covered native composer composite and its pointer region without resizing the original material contour or foreground. Focusing the composer dismisses the preview and preserves the draft.

Adding DECODEX_VISUAL_NATIVE_NAVIGATION to the isolated native composer probe exercises the shared hover entry and departure path. Its native rendering trace includes foreground ancestor mask geometry; this is separate from installed-app visual acceptance.

One PanelFrame samples layout slots and visible sidebar widths for each workspace frame. During opening, closing and reversal, the hover preview sits above the workspace and uses one edge to clip covered GPUI content, including the center fill and composer footer, and the native composer. The native composer applies its mask during parent prepaint. Attached native material surfaces respect the parent viewport for drawing and pointer input.
Deleting a Project removes its registration and keeps conversations, Work and files. Its independent active conversations appear in Chats.

The sidebar uses a shared 28-point leading slot for utility, category, project and conversation rows. With equal 6-point insets, the 40-point compact rail centers category and utility icons plus project and conversation initials. Title suffixes remain fully clipped, and expanded rows retain one text origin.
Codex conversations can register an external native thread as an independent Agent or under an existing Agent. The catalog reuses the shared overlay.

Archive groups and titles align with the search text. Project metadata and time share the row alignment. The selection control joins the actions. Narrow rows can wrap the project name below the title.

A live desktop window keeps its own selected conversation during shared draft reconciliation. Draft contents stay with their original conversation. A cold start can use the persisted editor selection.
